data.summary: The two‑week plan focuses on the weak Unit 6 first, then covers the remaining units, ending with a mixed review. Each week uses the full 10 hours, with concrete tasks that can be completed in one sitting.

weeks.focus: Master Unit 6 and review key concepts from Units 1–5
tasks: Do 15 Riemann sum practice problems, then check solutions and note common mistakes.
Solve 10 definite integral problems using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, marking each step.
Create a summary sheet of the Fundamental Theorem, including conditions and notation.
Do 5 limit problems from 1.2–1.5, then write a short explanation of each technique used.
Do 5 derivative problems from 2.1–2.5, then reflect on the power rule and its applications.

weeks.focus: Review all units and practice timed problem sets
tasks: Do a 30‑minute timed quiz covering Units 3–5, then review errors.
Do a 30‑minute timed quiz covering Units 7–8, then review errors.
Do 10 mixed‑topic free‑response questions (one from each unit), marking them against the scoring guide.
Create a one‑page cheat sheet of key formulas and theorems from all units.
Simulate a full exam with 60 minutes of practice questions, then analyze performance and adjust study focus.

data.final_week_advice: Use the last week for a full-length timed practice and targeted review of any remaining weak spots before the exam.
